what: Foursquare OS Places category label -> Mot Dang cat/sub. Ordered; first match wins.
why: Foursquare publishes hierarchical labels ('Dining and Drinking > Restaurant > Asian Restaurant > Thai Restaurant'), not slugs, so the rules match on the label text. As with overture_categories.json this DELIBERATELY does not map everything: a category with no row here admits no record. Unmapped rows are counted and named in the run's review file so the gap is visible rather than silent.
measured: Against the 2024 mirror restricted to a CM/CR postcode, still trading and not already ours: 35,310 rows. Dining 18,049 - retail 4,555 - community and government 4,261 - business services 4,120 - travel 3,026 - landmarks 1,685 - health 866 - arts 693 - sport 425 - events 58.

rules.match: > Food Truck|> Food Stand|> Street Food
> Transport Hub|> Bus Station|> Train Station
> Gym and Studio|> Sports and Recreation > Gym
> Waterfall|> Scenic Lookout|> Hot Spring|> Mountain|> National Park

deliberately_unmapped.Community and Government > Residential B: 1,107 rows. A block of flats is not a place a reader looks up, and realestate/condo is fed by the Treasury condominium register, which has unit counts and a juristic person. Admitting these would bury that shelf in unnamed buildings.
deliberately_unmapped.Business and Professional Services > Off: 959 rows. 'Office' names no trade. DBD's TSIC codes say what a company actually does; this label does not.
deliberately_unmapped.Community and Government > Housing Devel: 238 rows. Same reason as Residential Building.
deliberately_unmapped.Landmarks and Outdoors > Structure: 434 rows. A bridge, a pylon, a gate. The Edge survey models named ways and structures separately.
deliberately_unmapped.Landmarks and Outdoors > States and Muni: 176 rows. An admin area, not a place. crawl_admin.py owns these.
deliberately_unmapped.Community and Government > Government Bu: 407 rows. civic exists but the label does not say which office, and citizeninfo does.
